newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdog urges water firms to stem leakage.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdog urges water firms to stem leakage.

text.p: British water industry watchdog Ofwat said on Wednesday that water companies have not improved their positions on water leakage satisfactorily in the year 1995/1996 while they have progressed in unit cost efficiency.

"The companies report little reduction in leakage," Ofwat's 1995-96 report on the cost of water delivery and sewage collection, said. "Some companies will need to work harder to meet the targets they set for themselves next year," it said.
However, for the first time since the privatisation of water services companies, the unit cost of delivery water to customers has fallen, the report said.
"The cost of delivering water fell in real terms because of increased output," it said, adding that the costs went down to 59 pence per cubic metre in 1995-96 from 62 pence in 1994-95.

Another positive factor was that the unit cost of collecting sewage rose only modestly, by one and a half percent to 81 pence per cubic metre from 80 pence in 1994-95, despite a large and growing capital investment programme.
Late last month an other report by Ofwat said that capital investment by the water and sewerage companies in the core business totalled 2.6 billion stg in 1995-96.
Unit operating costs fell in real terms for both water and sewage services in the year 1995-96 and customers are expected to take advantage of this next year.

"These latest figures show that incentive regulation is working...These efficiencies will be passed to customers at the next price review," Ian Byatt, Director General of Water Services, said. Ofwat's figures showed that the total volume of water delivered in the year 1995-96 rose by more than four percent over the previous year due to the unusually hot and dry whether last summer. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 7717
